question: Should user-defined shortcut discovery in WebChat be owned by existing command metadata, a new first-party shortcut config/storage surface, or the broader plugin Control UI contribution-slot work?
rationale: Current main has slash-command discovery and plugin sidebar tabs, but the requested click-to-insert prompt snippets would add either new core config/storage semantics or new plugin/UI API semantics, and repository direction prefers lean core and plugin-owned optional capability when feasible.

options.title: Use Command Metadata First
options.body: Build the first version as a Control UI browser over existing built-in, skill, and plugin command metadata, adding prompt insertion only where the metadata can safely express it.

options.title: Approve First-Party Shortcuts
options.body: Add a `webchat.shortcuts` or equivalent storage contract with schema, docs, UI, and upgrade tests despite the larger config surface.

options.title: Wait For Plugin Contribution Slots
options.body: Defer implementation until the Control UI contribution-slot RFC settles a manifest/plugin panel shape that can host shortcut browsing outside core.

recommendation.title: Use Command Metadata First
recommendation.body: Build the first version as a Control UI browser over existing built-in, skill, and plugin command metadata, adding prompt insertion only where the metadata can safely express it.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the current chat composer, command discovery, and plugin tab surfaces where steipete has the strongest recent current-main history signal.
